commits.title: Database flags: eight rules over two daily readings, as pure code with a test each

changes.how: Pure: no import of server code, zod or the database. Types: StatementReading = { key: string (the statement's id in the reading: its queryid, or a hash of its text), text: string, calls: number, totalMs: number, meanMs: number, rows: number }; TableReading = { name: string, rows: number, bytes: number, seqScans: number, seqRowsRead: number }; IndexReading = { table: string, name: string, scans: number, backsConstraint: boolean }; JobReading = { job: string, runs: number, worked: number | null }; AiReading = { feature: string, figure: string, value: number, bar: number, daysOver: number }; DailyReading = { day: string, statements: StatementReading[] (the 40 costliest and the 40 most called, without repeats), tables: TableReading[], schemas: { name: string, bytes: number }[], indexes: IndexReading[], jobs: JobReading[], ai: AiReading[] }. Export the two written lists as constants with a reason per entry: WHOLE_READ_ALLOWED: at most 5 { table, reason } entries (start empty) and COSTLY_ALLOWED: { key, reason, ceilingMs }[] (start empty; at most 3 when the plan ends: a comment says so). Export HOT_TABLES = ['orders','order_lines','visits','products','product_variants','customers','carts','cart_lines'] (CLAUDE.md's list). Export type PlatformFlag = { id: FlagId, subject: string, values: Record<string, string | number> } and FLAG_IDS = ['new_top_statement','whole_table_read','idle_write','cron_schema_large','unused_hot_index','costly_statement','idle_route_calls','ai_over_bar']. Export platformFlags(today: DailyReading, yesterday: DailyReading, options: { openedOn: string | null, cronSchemaMaxBytes: number (default 80 MB; step 3.1 lowers it to 20 MB), idleCallsOn: boolean (default false; step 3.3 switches it on) }): PlatformFlag[]. The day's difference of a counter is today's value minus yesterday's, and 0 when negative (the statistics were reset). A difference exists only for a key present in BOTH readings (a statement by key, a table by name, a job by job, an index by table and name): yesterday's reading holds only 80 statements, so a statement absent yesterday has no difference and rules 2, 3, 6 and 7 and dayDifference() skip it (never treat yesterday's value as 0: its cumulative counter would raise false flags); rule 1 alone looks at statements absent yesterday. A job whose worked is null today or yesterday is skipped by rule 7. Rules: (1) new_top_statement: a statement among today's 25 highest by calls (today's cumulative calls, since it has no difference) whose key is not in yesterday's reading at all. (2) whole_table_read: a table with rows over 500 whose seqScans difference is over 10, unless WHOLE_READ_ALLOWED names it. (3) idle_write: a statement whose text starts with update, delete or insert (case-insensitive, after trimming), with a calls-difference of at least 10, whose rows-difference is under one tenth of its calls-difference. (4) cron_schema_large: the schema 'cron' over options.cronSchemaMaxBytes. (5) unused_hot_index: only when options.openedOn is at least 56 days before today.day: an index on a HOT_TABLES table with scans 0 today and backsConstraint false. (6) costly_statement: a statement among today's 40 highest by totalMs-difference with a calls-difference over 10 and (totalMs-difference divided by calls-difference) over 5, unless COSTLY_ALLOWED names its key and its mean is at or under that entry's ceilingMs. (7) idle_route_calls: only when options.idleCallsOn: the sum over jobs whose name starts with 'route.' of (runs-difference minus worked-difference) over 1,100. (8) ai_over_bar: an AiReading with value over bar and daysOver at least 7. Export dayDifference(today, yesterday): the rows the screen shows: per schema the bytes change, the 10 statements with the largest totalMs-difference, the 10 tables with the largest seqRowsRead-difference.

One test per rule with a small hand-made pair of readings, each with the case that raises the flag and the nearest case that does not: an 8 ms statement run 20 times raises costly_statement and the same at 4 ms does not; a 600-row table scanned 20 times raises whole_table_read, 400 rows does not, and the same table named in an allowed list passed as a parameter does not; an update called 100 times that changed 5 rows raises idle_write and one that changed 50 does not; a statement new among the top 25 raises new_top_statement; the cron schema at 81 MB raises, at 79 MB not, and at 21 MB with cronSchemaMaxBytes 20 MB raises; an unused index on orders raises only when openedOn is 56 days or more before and it backs no constraint; 1,200 idle route calls raise only with idleCallsOn; an AI figure over its bar for 7 days raises and for 6 does not. One test that a counter that went down (a reset) gives a difference of 0 and no flag. One test that WHOLE_READ_ALLOWED has at most 5 entries and COSTLY_ALLOWED at most 3, each with a reason of at least 20 characters. Add one more test: a statement in today's reading with 1,000,000 calls and a mean of 50 ms that is absent from yesterday's raises new_top_statement only, not costly_statement or idle_write (no difference is taken against a missing row).

commits.title: The daily reading also keeps the hot tables' indexes and each scheduled job's runs

changes.how: Step 0.2 made commerce.platform_readings (day, kind, name, figures jsonb, query) with the check platform_readings_kind: kind in ('statement', 'table', 'schema'). Widen that one check to: kind in ('statement', 'table', 'schema', 'index', 'job', 'ai'). Change nothing else of the table. Extend its doc comment: for kind index, name is '<table>.<index>' and figures hold scans and backs_constraint; for kind job, name is the ledger's job key and figures hold runs and worked (null until step 3.3); for kind ai, name is '<feature>.<figure>' and figures hold value, bar and days_over (written from step 1.19's follow-up on).

Generated: run 'pnpm db:generate' after the schema edit. Drizzle writes a drop of the check platform_readings_kind and an add of the wider one. Read the file: it must hold only those two statements on commerce.platform_readings. Commit the new snapshot with it. Do not write it by hand.

Step 0.2 creates this file: recordProductionReading(now) runs one db().transaction with three inserts into commerce.platform_readings (kind 'table', 'schema', and 'statement' when pg_stat_statements can be read), each `on conflict (day, kind, name) do nothing returning 1`, and returns `Promise<{ tables: number; schemas: number; statements: number }>`; beside it pruneProductionReadings(). Extend recordProductionReading() with two more inserts inside the same transaction, after the schema insert, in the same form as its 'table' insert: (a) kind 'index': `insert into commerce.platform_readings (day, kind, name, figures) select <day>::date, 'index', i.relname || '.' || i.indexrelname, jsonb_build_object('scans', i.idx_scan, 'backs_constraint', exists (select 1 from pg_constraint c where c.conindid = i.indexrelid)) from pg_stat_user_indexes i where i.schemaname = 'commerce' and i.relname in ('orders', 'order_lines', 'visits', 'products', 'product_variants', 'customers', 'carts', 'cart_lines') on conflict (day, kind, name) do nothing returning 1`; (b) kind 'job': `insert into commerce.platform_readings (day, kind, name, figures) select <day>::date, 'job', j.job, jsonb_build_object('runs', j.runs, 'worked', null) from commerce.cron_jobs j on conflict (day, kind, name) do nothing returning 1` (commerce.cron_jobs has runs but no 'worked' column yet; step 3.3 adds it and changes this line). Use the same `<day>` value the function's other inserts use. Add `indexes` and `jobs` (the number of rows each insert returned) to the returned object and to the function's return type. src/app/api/cron/subscription-reminders/route.ts does not change: step 0.2 spreads the function's result into the job's answer, so the two new counts appear there by themselves.

Server-only. Export latestReadings(): reads the two newest days of commerce.platform_readings (day, kind, name, figures, query) through typedRows() with a zod row (col helpers from src/server/typed-rows.ts; figures as z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())) and maps them to the DailyReading type of src/lib/platform-flags.ts: a 'statement' row gives { key: name, text: query, calls, totalMs: figures.total_ms, meanMs: figures.mean_ms, rows }; a 'table' row { name, rows, bytes, seqScans: figures.seq_scan, seqRowsRead: figures.seq_tup_read }; a 'schema' row { name, bytes }; an 'index' row { table and index split from name at the first dot, scans, backsConstraint }; a 'job' row { job: name, runs, worked }; an 'ai' row { feature and figure split from name, value, bar, daysOver }. A kind with no rows is an empty list. Export currentFlags(now = new Date(), options: { openedOn?: string | null; idleCallsOn?: boolean; cronSchemaMaxBytes?: number } = {}): returns { today, yesterday, flags: platformFlags(today, yesterday, { openedOn: options.openedOn ?? null, idleCallsOn: options.idleCallsOn ?? false, cronSchemaMaxBytes: options.cronSchemaMaxBytes ?? 80 * 1024 * 1024 }), difference: dayDifference(...) } or null when fewer than two days are stored. No table holds an opening date today (commerce.platform_settings has none, and step 0.2 adds none), so the screen and the briefing call currentFlags() with no options and flag five stays off: say so in a comment above the function, naming the step that will pass an opening date when it exists. Read no other table for it. It never throws: on an error it logs 'platform_flags.failed' through log() and returns null. Include the platform's own rows: the reading is of the whole database, so Kaizena Flow's store and null-store rows are counted with every other; add no store filter.

Seeds two days into commerce.platform_readings directly (insert rows of each kind with the figures keys named above) and asserts currentFlags() returns each of the eight flags for its seeded case: a statement at 8 ms run 20 times; a 600-row table scanned 20 times; an update called 100 times with 5 rows; the cron schema at 81 MB; an unused index on orders, with `currentFlags(now, { openedOn: <the date 60 days before the seeded today> })`; a statement new in the top 25; 1,200 idle route calls, with `currentFlags(now, { idleCallsOn: true })` and two 'job' rows named 'route.<something>' whose worked figures are numbers (not null) on both days; an AI figure over its bar for 7 days. Then one case with a single stored day: currentFlags() returns null. Then one case that runs recordProductionReading() on the test database and asserts the day has an 'index' row for every index of commerce.orders and a 'job' row for every row of commerce.cron_jobs. Clean up the seeded days in afterAll.
